pages.heading: KNCraft Architecture
pages.body: Portals, tents and survival work together. This chapter explains the new options. Survival additions start disabled; use $(bold)/kncraft status$() to check this server. Sewing and food tooltips show the active values.

pages.heading: Prepare together
pages.body: Grow cotton, sew clothing, cook provisions and pack a tent before an expedition. Farming and hunting offer different supplies. Meals offer brief help; keep your waterskin, shelter and specialized clothing.

pages.heading: Cotton lining
pages.body: When cotton insulation is enabled, Pam's cotton works in the Sewing Table. Default: 1 cold / 0.5 heat insulation. It uses normal Cold Sweat slots and removal rules. Cotton does not count as wool in unrelated recipes.

pages.heading: Wildlife materials
pages.body: With wildlife insulation enabled: bear fur gives 1.5 cold, bison fur 1.75 cold, and kangaroo hide 0.75 cold / 0.75 heat. These defaults leave goat fur, hoglin hide and adaptive materials useful.

pages.heading: Frontier Cap
pages.body: The wildlife option gives the worn Frontier Cap 3 cold / 1 heat insulation by default. Built-in insulation consumes sewing capacity. Cold Sweat still owns your existing armor and sewn linings. Check its tooltip before adding more.

pages.heading: Warm provisions
pages.body: With thermal meals enabled, hot tea, coffee and nettle tea provide +0.2 base temperature for 60 seconds. Carrot soup, potato soup and stew last 90 seconds at the same strength. These are the default settings.

pages.heading: Cool provisions
pages.body: Melon smoothie and ice cream provide -0.2 base temperature for 60 seconds. Apple juice gives a lighter -0.1 for 30 seconds. Values are Cold Sweat temperature units, not instant body-temperature points.

pages.heading: One meal effect
pages.body: KNCraft meals share one active effect: the latest replaces the previous, including hot versus cold meals. Repeating a meal refreshes its time. Normal hunger and container rules still apply; food is not a replacement for a waterskin.

pages.heading: Backpack feeding
pages.body: Pam's hot tea cannot be consumed at full hunger in the tested pack. A feeding upgrade chooses for hunger, not temperature. Pack deliberate hot/cold supplies; automatic temperature-based selection is not part of this update.

pages.heading: Cotton canvas
pages.body: With fiber recipes enabled, surround one wool block with eight cotton to make tent canvas. Wool can itself come from cotton-made string. This costs the same fiber as the original cotton-to-string-to-wool route. Find the pattern in JEI.

pages.heading: Plant rope
pages.body: Six cotton and three vines make eight RopeBridge ropes when fiber recipes are enabled. Use rows cotton/cotton/vine, vine/cotton/cotton, cotton/cotton/vine. This replaces three string with six cotton at the original cost.

pages.heading: Native portals
pages.body: Light Aether and Depth frames with their normal items. Successful lighting converts to an immersive pair; stick activation remains a fallback. Failed conversion preserves native travel. Existing pairs stay where players built them.

pages.heading: Depth arrivals
pages.body: New Depth frames and their landing rooms stay between Y=5 and Y=122. The adapter avoids bedrock, fluids, block entities and occupied rooms. A failed safe placement restores the native source portal.

pages.heading: Tent crossings
pages.body: Complete tents get seamless entrances while keeping Nomadic Tents ownership and contents. New interiors wait for connected clients to acknowledge the dimension. If an entrance stays closed, reconnect a stalled client or use the native door.

pages.heading: Pack and move
pages.body: Use the physical door to pack a tent. Old links are invalidated when it is packed, damaged or moved. Quick return crossings remain possible. Turning off immersive entrances retains the dimension synchronization repair.

pages.heading: Explore the network
pages.body: Natural Waystones remain protected travel infrastructure. Their crafting and drops stay restricted. Wither Storm encounter scaling happens once; revisiting or reloading an already balanced encounter does not heal it again.

pages.heading: Keep this guide
pages.body: Craft a book with one paper to get this Field Guide. The matching KNCraft Architecture mod supplies its chapters and artwork to each player. Existing books keep the same identity and bookmarks.
